recentItems.title: Bill aims to draw a red line on human rights breaches
recentItems.description:
Pressure is piling on the federal government to limit its possible involvement in genocide or war crimes.

Drafted by international legal experts, crossbenchers have introduced the Red Lines bill – a world-first suite of measures which would block Australia's defence exports or trade with countries found to be breaching international law.

recentItems.title: Trump dismisses fears that AI could destroy humanity as a ‘hoax’
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump has said the only guardrail that AI needs a is a "high IQ President" and dismissed calls that "AI is going to take over the world" as a "hoax".

Pressure to act on AI regulation has grown over the past week, following dire warnings from leading AI executives regarding concerns over human ability to control the technology.

The US president has brushed those concerns aside, saying that the US needs to maintain a competitive edge with China. 

China’s foreign ministry has spoken out against what it calls “fearmongering” and “vicious competition” over AI governance.  

For more on this story: https://bit.ly/4gRUOMm

recentItems.title: Debate over Whyalla steelworks failure heats up
recentItems.description:
South Australia’s Whyalla is coming to terms with hundreds of workers losing their jobs following the decision to close the blast furnace at the city’s steelworks. 

The decision, which will see the loss of more than 500 jobs, is fuelling the political debate around the future of manufacturing.

recentItems.title: Hanson offers qualified apology over Indigenous Australians remarks
recentItems.description:
The federal government is facing a warning that fruit will rot on the ground unless Prime Minister Anthony Albanese intervenes to clear the bottleneck of pending applications for working holiday visas.

One Nation has promised backpackers would be carved out of its migration restrictions.

It comes as the party’s leader, Pauline Hanson, has issued a qualified apology for comments she made about Indigenous Australians.

recentItems.title: Russia-Ukraine partial energy ceasefire | Houthis claim more islands | Trump rejects AI safeguards
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed not to hit each other's energy targets.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says he's prepared to halt strikes but doubts Russia will do the same.

Targeted strikes have raised doubts, with Kyiv's mayor reporting a Russian strike on a petrol station in the capital today. 

In Russia a missile attack damaged a building of an e-commerce company in the port city of Taganrog.

recentItems.title: Hanson condemned over resurfaced remarks about Indigenous culture
recentItems.description:
Pauline Hanson has been slammed as "completely racist" after she labelled Indigenous Australians "the most primitive race on Earth".

The One Nation leader made the comments during an interview with the JJ Podcast a year ago, where she criticised the study of Indigenous history in schools.

Independent senator Lidia Thorpe urged Hanson to consider the "real harm" her commentary could cause.

Labor cabinet minister Tanya Plibersek said on News24 there seemed to be no limit to who Hanson was willing to "kick down", and questioned the basis of her comments on Indigenous culture.

When pressed by journalists as to whether she would apologise for her comments Hanson said, 'If I’ve offended people by using that [word], yes, I will apologise for that'.

Read more: https://bit.ly/4ipRKbu

recentItems.title: Houthi-Saudi conflict escalates in Yemen
recentItems.description:
Conflict in Yemen is entering a new phase, with Houthi positions along the Red Sea coming under bombardment by Saudi Arabia, according to the rebel group. 

Facing retaliatory strikes, Saudi Arabia's civil defence issued, but since lifted, warnings of potential danger in four cities. 

In advances following a week-long offensive, the Houthis seized the Yemeni side of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, one of the world's most important shipping arteries and the southern gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, threatening Saudi oil exports diverted from the Strait of Hormuz.

Hundreds have been killed and tens of thousands displaced as rebel Houthi forces in Yemen advanced on key cities.

recentItems.title: Trump rejects tech industry’s calls for AI slowdown
recentItems.description:
US President Donald Trump has brushed aside concerns raised by AI leaders – including Elon Musk, Dario Amodei and Sam Altman – about the pace of its development, branding them "very negative forces".

Trump says the US must maintain its dominance over China in artificial intelligence, despite dire warnings from insiders it could lead to the extinction of the human race.

As the AI alarm bells continue to grow louder, Australia's government says it’s taking these calls from the tech industry for a slowdown seriously.

recentItems.title: New bill seeks consistent definition of affordable housing
recentItems.description:
New federal legislation is seeking to make the definition of affordable housing consistent across the country.

Independent MP Nicolette Boele has introduced a bill to make sure renters, including frontline workers, can rely on the definition of affordable.

The move has been welcomed by housing groups and the property industry.
